memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"(The LORD made the Egyptians favorably disposed toward the people, and Moses
himself was highly regarded in Egypt by Pharaoh's officials and by the people.)"
- Ex 11:3 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Here is a small verse doing a big work. How would slaves ever get silver and
gold from their masters? God answers that question before it is asked. He
changes the hearts of the Egyptians.

Think about what has just happened in Egypt. Blood in the water, frogs,
darkness, hail, boils. By any human calculation, the Egyptians should hate the
Israelites and hate Moses most of all. Instead, God gives His people favour in
the eyes of the very people who oppressed them.

This is the quiet work of God that we rarely see happening. He was not only
sending plagues on Pharaoh; He was softening ordinary Egyptian hearts at the
same time. Two things were going on at once, and only one of them was visible.

We often assume God is only working in the loud, obvious places. But He is also
at work in the boardroom where a decision is being made about you, in the mind
of the person who has been difficult, in circumstances you cannot influence at
all. Joseph experienced this in Potiphar's house and in prison (Gen 39:21).
Daniel experienced it in Babylon.

You do not have to manufacture favour. You can ask God for it, do your work
honestly, and leave the hearts of others to Him.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Where do you need favour that you cannot arrange for yourself?
2. Have you thanked God for doors that opened without your effort?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, You hold the hearts of people in Your hand. Grant me favour where I need
it, and help me to walk with integrity so that my life honours You. Amen.
